scenes.text: Press start on the real mission that put people on the Moon: Apollo 11.
July 16, 1969. A Saturn V rocket launches three astronauts from Florida.
For about three days, the crew coasts across space toward the Moon.
Alarms flash and fuel runs low, but the lander Eagle touches down on July 20.
Four days later, the capsule splashes down safely in the Pacific Ocean.

levels.name: Liftoff
levels.text: A Saturn V rocket lifts off from Kennedy Space Center, Florida, with three astronauts.

levels.name: To the Moon
levels.text: The crew travels about 384,000 km to reach the Moon in roughly three days.

levels.name: The Eagle Lands
levels.text: Program alarms and low fuel, yet Eagle lands in the Sea of Tranquility on July 20.

levels.name: Splashdown
levels.text: On July 24, 1969 the Columbia capsule splashes down in the Pacific Ocean.
